newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac popularity up in French "cohabitation"-poll.
newsitem.headline: Chirac popularity up in French "cohabitation"-poll.

text.p: French conservative President Jacques Chirac's popularity has risen to its highest level since early 1996, apparently buoyed by power-sharing with a new Socialist government, an opinion poll showed on Tuesday.

The BVA institute survey for the weekly Paris Match showed that 48 percent of those quizzed had a good impression of Chirac as president, up from 40 percent in May. The number with a bad impression fell to 44 percent from 55.
It was the first time that Chirac had had a positive rating since April 1996.
Romain Pache, director of political studies at BVA, said Chirac's rise confirmed a rule that "cohabitation", or power-sharing between left and right, bolstered the president.

"This rule is based on a simple principle: in a period of cohabitation, at least at the start, the president benefits from an image of greater consensus," he wrote. France had two previous bouts of cohabitation in 1986-88 and 1993-95.

New Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who came to power in an upset election victory on June 1, was rated a good premier by 52 percent of the 1,017 people who responded to the poll, taken on July 17-19. Thirty percent rated him bad.
In May, just 30 percent had a good impression of his predecessor as premier, Chirac's ally Alain Juppe.
The number of people dissatisfied with the way France is governed fell to 62 percent in the latest poll from 75 percent two months ago.

And 51 percent judged cohabitation a good thing, against 48 percent at the start of the first cohabitation in May 1986 when late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand was forced to share power with Chirac, then prime minister.
